# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 79 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 79 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_079_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 2

**1** Among these the angel commanded that crowns be brought; palm-branch crowns were brought, and the angel crowned those who had given back completely green rods and sent them into the tower. **2** He also sent into the tower those whose rods were green but cracked, and he gave them seals. **3** All who went into the tower wore the same garment — white as snow. **4** He also sent away those who had returned rods half-green and half-withered, giving them clothing and seals. **5** As for those who gave back rods that were withered and moth-eaten — these were apostates: those who had betrayed the church and blasphemed the Lord through their shameful deeds, and were ashamed of the name of the Lord by which they had been called. These therefore perished utterly. **6** Those whose rods were withered but not moth-eaten — these had heard the word but remained in their sins without repenting. Those who returned rods half-green and half-withered are people occupied with business who do not attach themselves to the saints; therefore half of them is living and half is dead. **7** Those who brought rods two-thirds green and one-third withered are those who denied the faith, and denied it many times. **8** Those who returned rods two-thirds withered and one-third green — these are men who believed, but for the most part have lived in iniquity and wickedness, though some portion of righteousness remains in them. **9** Those who returned nearly all green rods with only the tip withered — these believed truly and are faithful, but carry slight blemishes. **10** Those who returned completely withered rods — these have already apostatized and do not repent, nor will they repent, on account of the hardness of their hearts; therefore the spirit of the Lord departed from them.

---

### Translator's Note
This chapter provides the key to Similitude 8's allegory. The ten categories of branches correspond to ten spiritual conditions of baptized Christians. The crucial insight is that even many of those in compromised states (categories 3-8) can still be restored through repentance — a central theme of the entire Shepherd. Only the completely withered (category 1) and the completely moth-eaten (category 10 reversed) are beyond hope. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout, with PNEUMA's "utterly" in v. 5 adopted.
